turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. Owen's zero went into the gradebook, and I found out from my son's phone in the middle of class. Who decided that, and before or after anyone spoke to him?
I appreciate you coming in with an open mind.
I haven't said anything yet that required an open mind. I came in with a question, and I'm still waiting on the answer. Who decided on the zero?
A lot of parents in your position would have gone straight to the principal. You didn't. That says a lot about you.
Don't manage me. I came to hear what you have, so what do you have?
So I'd like to keep this between us and keep it friendly. Deal?
Friendly is fine, but nothing in here stays between us. Whatever gets said goes in an email, and the principal is on it. What do you have on Owen's essay?
